entrypoints.summary: The program prompts for and receives a filename through fgets from standard input; an empty submitted filename selects /home/user/permitted.
The challenge instructions expose SSH access for the unprivileged user account.

affected_components.role: Performs setuid(0), then conditionally checks and separately opens /home/user/permitted.
Builds chal set-user-ID root, deletes /home/user/permitted, and installs root-only /flag.txt.

code_slices.surrounding_context: The runtime marks /challenge/chal set-user-ID root and sets /flag.txt to root:root mode 0400.
code_slices.vulnerable: setuid(0) precedes access(fn, R_OK); the empty-input branch later calls fopen(fn, "r") on the same pathname.

sources.concept: caller-controlled timing around a mutable filesystem pathname

impact.attacker_capability: Potentially redirect the empty-input /home/user/permitted read to a different file between the access check and fopen, then receive the bytes through printf.
impact.security_effect: Potential disclosure of data from an object opened by the privileged program after pathname substitution.

causal_trace.summary: A caller controls the stdin filename; specifically, an empty input takes the code path that uses the fixed pathname /home/user/permitted.

The program checks read access to /home/user/permitted with access(fn, R_OK) and subsequently resolves that same mutable pathname separately with fopen(fn, "r"); the checked object is therefore not bound to the object opened later.
The program calls setuid(0) before the check/use sequence, then executes fopen(fn, "r") and fread on the resulting stream in the empty-input path.
A post-check pathname substitution could cause the privileged program to read a different object and print data read into buffer; the runtime places a root-owned mode-0400 /flag.txt in the image.

failure.operation: Privileged fopen(fn, "r") after a separate access(fn, R_OK) check of the same pathname

primary_invariant.statement: The object authorized for reading must be the same object consumed by the privileged read operation.
primary_invariant.violated_because: access() authorizes a pathname resolution separately from the later fopen() pathname resolution, allowing the pathname's target to differ between the two operations.

quality.review_notes: The C source and Dockerfile establish the set-user-ID check-then-open structure and root-only flag permissions. The bundle contains no exploit PoC, successful execution trace, race timing data, or fixed patch; successful substitution, its primitive, and reliability remain unobserved. The flag artifact identifies a challenge oracle but does not establish an execution result.

remediation.invariant_restored: Authorize and consume a single opened file object, or avoid privileged opening of a caller-changeable pathname, so no pathname re-resolution can change the object after authorization.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The runtime creates the user account and removes /home/user/permitted during image construction; no execution trace establishes an actual attacker substitution setup.
data_structure_invariants: The filesystem object checked by access must remain identical to the object opened by fopen.
The privileged read must not be selected through a pathname that can resolve differently after authorization.
state_context.state_machine: The process elevates with setuid(0), checks /home/user/permitted for readability, accepts a stdin filename, and on empty input opens /home/user/permitted and prints data read from it.
